cohort: A total of 1497 children, including 535 preadolescents (10-12 years) and 962 adolescents (13-18 years), participated in the study.
finding: The study found a significant association between prematurity (28-32 weeks) and FGIDs, specifically functional nausea, but concluded overall that Cesarean delivery and prematurity are not general risk factors for the development of FGIDs.
mod_finding: There was no significant increase in the prevalence of any Rome IV FGIDs for children born via Cesarean delivery compared with vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from preadolescents (10-12 years) and adolescents (13-18 years) at the time of the survey.
